en: This prayer is established as a gateway of skillful means because the vow to benefit sentient beings within this Sahā world is made;
through the construction of wisdom reaching the eight directions, the sounds of peace and bliss compete to come forth, and the Brahma-kings hasten to welcome [the practitioner].

The aforementioned intention is that the burdens of tenant laborers are difficult to dispel, and demonic influences and ghostly hauntings extend for thousands of *li*. [May these be] warded off at the gates of the earth; may all these manifold virtues not limit auspicious conditions. First, [may the merits] be employed [for this purpose]. May the majestic radiance of the Four Heavenly Kings, the Dragon Deities, and the Eight Divisions of Spirits blaze forth, and may their power of blessing increase ever more. May they arise to save sentient beings and protect the state. Furthermore, with these superior blessings, I next employ them to adorn my [position as] Prefect of Hexi.
May the Great King [Name] hold his noble station.
We humbly pray that he may be as venerable as the Southern Dipper and the Northern Pole,
serving as a Bodhisattva among kings.
Forever responding to the entrustment of the Tathāgata,
you further uphold supreme merit to adorn your station as the Honored Master,
the Chief Monk of the Hexi Commandery.
I humbly pray that your governance and administration may be firmly established, and that your physical vigor remain as steadfast as a mountain.
May your life be prolonged for a vast duration, and may you successively attain supreme merit. Furthermore, I pray that you continue to direct the honorable office of the Minister of State.

I humbly pray that the golden branches may flourish forever and the jade leaves remain perpetually fragrant; that the fragrant influence of the Pan-shih (Boulder) shall increase and the Wei-cheng (Walled City) shall serve as a guardian bulwark.
Furthermore, may this superior merit be employed next to adorn the noble positions of the Commandant of the Yandu, the Commandant of the Xunduyu, and the various Commanders-in-Chief.

I humbly pray that men of extraordinary talent will emerge from among the masses and those of unexcelled skill will be summoned to return to Your embrace; that those capable of governing the world may together assist in the Way of the Enlightened King.
Only then will all under heaven be settled and the realm within the seas be purified.
There is no record of his name in the annals of war;
he relied instead upon the protection of the Dharma.
The Mahāprajñāpāramitā brings boundless benefit and joy.
The Great Assembly reverently recites this universally. □□□□ □□□□ Dao□□ Record.
